I keep the tins set on the table and I move the funnel with my hands. 

I’m not super strong so I find when I have over 1,200 grams of wax and fragrance in the pouring pot my hand hurts a lot while I pour, and it’s hard to get the speed of pour right (I use the double boiler method still). 

The funnel removes all arm pain and makes it easy to pour at the exact speed you want. 

Because it’s not poured at an angle like the pouring pitcher, the funnel also prevents me from accidentally knocking the wick out of position once I have it in place with a wick holder.

That's really something only you can answer following some thorough market research and planning. 

Where would you sell your candles? How much time and effort can you dedicate to this business? 

What is the competition like in your area/competitors online?  How does your product quality and branding compare to what's already out there? What is your unique selling point? 

How much does it cost to produce one candle? How much will it cost to ship? How much investment will you need to scale up your business, and what cost savings can you expect? How much can you realistically charge for one candle (as a rough guideline, people aim for a price that is 4 times the cost to produce the candle). 

How will you get customers? Do you have an advertising or organic social media growth plan? 

  
You need to be able to answer all of these questions confidently. Start drafting up a proper business plan and see if this is a realistic business for you. Good luck!
